reasons: The cited clause imposes a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation on Customer for the full term with no category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no performance-based exit — this fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory, so 'deviation' is correctly classified.

The redline reaches the preferred position (non-exclusive supply, express right to procure from third parties) while preserving the underlying supply arrangement; the high changed-character ratio is justified because the exclusivity grant itself must be reversed, and no residual requirements/sole-supplier language remains.

The comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, cites the playbook position, and correctly notes the conflict with Sections 2.1 and 12.3; no exclusivity benefiting Customer was removed.
